stem:
When answering this question it should be assumed that together all the hydrogen atoms in a benzene ring result in a single unsplit peak at $\delta = 7.2$ in a proton ($^1\text{H}$) NMR spectrum. The structures of five isomeric ketones, **P**, **Q**, **R**, **S** and **T** are given.

**P** $\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{COCH}(\text{CH}_3)_2$ **S** $\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{COCH}_3$

**Q** $\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{COCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$ **T** $\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)\text{COCH}_3$

**R** $\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CH}_2\text{COCH}_2\text{CH}_3$

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Identify all the chiral carbon atoms on the structures above. Label each chiral carbon atom with an asterisk (*).

parts.label: (b)
(b)(i)
parts.text: Identify which of the compounds **P**, **Q**, **R**, **S** or **T** gives this spectrum. Draw the displayed formula of the compound you have identified. Identify the protons responsible for the peaks at $\delta = 3.7$, $\delta = 2.5$ and $\delta = 1.0$ on the structure you have drawn.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: Name the splitting pattern of the peak at $\delta = 3.7$. Explain why it has this splitting pattern.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text: Choose from the letters **P**, **Q**, **R**, **S** and **T** to identify:

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.text: the **two** compounds that each have a doublet peak in the proton ($^1\text{H}$) NMR spectrum

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text: the compound with only three peaks in its proton ($^1\text{H}$) NMR spectrum.

parts.label: (d)
parts.text: Suggest a suitable solvent that should be used for obtaining the spectrum shown in Fig. 8.1.

parts.label: (e)
parts.text:
The proton ($^1\text{H}$) NMR spectrum of compound **T** is compared in the presence of $\text{D}_2\text{O}$ and in the absence of $\text{D}_2\text{O}$.

Describe any difference between the two spectra. Explain your answer.
